entries.name: CBOT Maize
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of CBOT Maize as of September 30 increased by 5.4% MOM and rose by 22.7% YOY to $204.78/MT. Market players linked the 5.4% month-on-month increase to tighter US and global supply expectations, with USDA cutting US production by 5.42 million mt as yields were revised lower. Sources added that global consumption is expected to exceed production by around 22 million mt, while further rainfall could temporarily slow the US harvest and delay physical availability. Harvest progress and South American weather remain key watchpoints into October.

entries.name: Indian Rice
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Indian Rice as of September 30 increased by 2.7% MOM and rose by 6.9% YOY to $385/MT. Market players linked the 2.7% month-on-month increase to tightening new-crop expectations after below-normal monsoon rainfall reduced yield potential. Industry estimates suggest India’s 2026 rice crop could fall by around 10 million mt year-on-year, while export prices reached their highest level in more than a year during September. Looking ahead, record government stocks should limit upside and maintain export availability despite the smaller crop.

Thai skipjack tuna continues to show upward pressure in price as landings in the Western Central Pacific Ocean have been reported as challenging. This is combined by increases in production costs associated with fuel and shipping freight, which are driving the current market sentiment. Similar price trends have been observed for Ecuadorian skipjack tuna.

entries.name: Chinese Apple
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Chinese Apple as of September 23 decreased by 0.4% MOM and rose by 0.1% YOY to $1.38/kg. This month, China’s apple market is moving from earlier firmness into a softer, more competitive phase. Imported apples had been supported by limited supply and steady quality, particularly from New Zealand, but domestic new-crop arrivals are now increasing and putting pressure on prices and sales. Holiday demand offered only selective support, favoring premium gift packs and better-quality fruit rather than lifting the broader market. After the festival, traffic and turnover slowed, and apple gift-box prices fell sharply. Overall, abundant supply, cautious buying, and weaker post-holiday demand are creating a softer market tone.

entries.name: Spanish Pear
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Spanish Pear as of September 23 decreased by 7.2% MOM and declined by 10.2% YOY to €1,670/MT. This month, Spain’s pear market remains challenging as the new season starts under heat-related pressure and weak commercial momentum. High summer temperatures are limiting fruit size and adding orchard-quality concerns, which is reducing the share of pears that meet preferred market specifications. Demand remains subdued, while overlap with Southern Hemisphere supply continues to weigh on early-season sales. As a result, more fruit is being placed into storage as exporters wait for better movement later in the campaign. Overall, the market remains cautious, with profitability tied to how quickly supply clears and whether autumn demand improves.

entries.name: Argentinian Pear
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Argentinian Pear as of September 2 was unchanged MOM and rose by 23.8% YOY to ARS 1,586.11/kg. This month, the Argentine pear market is being shaped by tighter export supply, export-readiness efforts, and a cautiously improving trade backdrop. A smaller crop has kept volumes lower, but the market has remained relatively orderly, with exporters focused on meeting phytosanitary and destination-market requirements. More broadly, Argentina’s pear sector is benefiting from somewhat improved macro conditions and better trade sentiment, though competitiveness is still constrained by logistics costs, currency dynamics, and structural cost pressures. Overall, the market remains stable but commercially disciplined rather than expansive.

This has contributed to a buildup of domestic supply.

entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Indian Onion as of September 30 increased by 38.8% MOM and rose by 116.5% YOY to INR 46,245.58/MT. Prices increased significantly throughout Q3, with market sources reporting significant storage losses. Unseasonal rain during the rabi harvest raised moisture content in the bulbs, and subsequent heat and humidity in June-July accelerated spoilage in stored stock. Some estimates put losses as high as 30-40% of stored rabi product. In addition, the kharif crop is reportedly delayed, due to late rainfall.

entries.name: ICE #11 Raw Sugar Futures
entries.paragraph: The average weekly spot price of ICE #11 Raw Sugar Futures as of September 30 increased by 0.4% MOM and rose by 13.7% YOY to USc 17.60/Lb. Overall, sugar price movements continued to be primarily driven by weather developments and forecast updates.

entries.name: ICE New York Arabica
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of ICE New York Arabica as of September 30 decreased by 22.2% MOM and declined by 22.6% YOY to USc 284.57/Lb. Arabica prices in September fell significantly, as earlier uncertainty in July and August around the pace of Brazilian arabica exports eased. Throughout September, Brazilian exports accelerated and by the end of the month, Brazil was on track for record September coffee exports, according to market sources. As the market started to see the expected supply arriving, prices eased. Furthermore, Brazil started to receive rainfall, aiding flowering for next year's crop, reducing some of the weather risk premium that had supported prices earlier on in the year.

Independent converters disputed the hikes and buyers reported ample supply, so little of the increase reached open-market contracts.

We also note that HRC prices have now reached a three-year high. Market sources in Europe point to import restrictions introduced in 2026 as the main driver of price growth. In the US, HRC prices also continued to rise in September, supported by tariff policy on imports.

HDPE posted the largest move among the polyolefins. •The uptick came despite comfortable domestic inventories and was supported in part by stronger export demand and a late-month crude oil rally tied to renewed Middle East tensions.

entries.name: Euronext Maize

USDA forecasts EU production at 50.6 million mt, down 10.9% year-on-year, increasing reliance on imports, while constrained Ukrainian export routes continue to limit nearby availability. Market players said EU import demand and the ability of Ukrainian grain to move through alternative routes will remain important price drivers.

entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Chinese Pear as of September 23 decreased by 0.5% MOM and declined by 8.6% YOY to CNY 5,960/MT. This month, China’s pear market remains under pressure as new-season supply builds faster than demand. A larger, generally good-quality crop is weighing on prices, while buyers are purchasing cautiously and showing limited interest in building stocks. Domestic consumption remains subdued, and exporters are also facing a more competitive environment shaped by shifting overseas demand, policy uncertainty, and logistics costs. Market sentiment across fresh produce remains cautious, with ample supply putting pressure on returns. As a result, more fruit may be held in storage, which could prolong supply pressure later in the marketing season if demand does not strengthen.

entries.name: US Cartonboard FBB
entries.paragraph: In September, the average price of US Cartonboard FBB was unchanged MOM and rose by 1.4% YOY to $0.70/Lb. In Europe, higher energy costs have led cartonboard makers to announce increases, including €89/t from Sappi effective November 1.

entries.name: LME Aluminium
entries.paragraph: In September, the average 3m futures price of LME Aluminium increased by 0.7% MOM and rose by 23.5% YOY to $3,272.89/MT. The metals market was balanced according to players due to a decline in speculative activity. Rising aluminum metals exports from China and gradual increase in aluminum metals exports from Persian Gulf countries allowed supply to increase. At the same time, demand for aluminum metals continues to be high.

entries.name: EU LDPE
entries.paragraph: In September, the average price of EU LDPE increased by 1.4% MOM and rose by 34.1% YOY to €2,532/MT. Most converters have been purchasing only near-term requirements, and the reopening of arbitrage, led by China's return to export markets, has begun to reshape global trade flows and pressure European offers.

entries.name: US LDPE
entries.paragraph: In September, the average price of US LDPE increased by 0.1% MOM and rose by 5.8% YOY to USc 97.60/Lb. LDPE edged up more modestly in September, with most of the gains resulting due to increases in export demand, according to sources.

entries.name: US PET
entries.paragraph: In September, the average price of US PET decreased by 1.7% MOM and rose by 6.9% YOY to USc 64.40/Lb. PET and PVC extended softer trends driven by measured downstream purchasing and ample supply.

entries.name: US PP
entries.paragraph: In September, the average price of US PP decreased by 5.2% MOM and declined by 7.9% YOY to USc 66.80/Lb. PP was pulled lower by declining PGP feedstock costs. The market has not weakened in a disorderly way, but domestic buying remains patient, with processors purchasing to cover near-term needs rather than building inventory.
